reason: Paper describes ZC3H7B-BCOR gene fusions in uterine endometrial stromal sarcomas. While BCOR is the gene of interest, the clinical subject is exclusively gynaecological oncology with no ophthalmic phenotype mentioned. The BCOR connection is through its cancer fusion role, not through its oculofaciocardiodental or Lenz microphthalmia syndrome relevance. Not useful for an ophthalmogenetics library.

Broad dental genetics review covering amelogenesis imperfecta, dentinogenesis imperfecta, and dental anomalies in multiple congenital anomaly syndromes. PubMed MeSH terms contain no ocular descriptors. Although BCOR-related OFCD syndrome has dental involvement, this review does not specifically address BCOR or OFCD, and the library focus is ophthalmic genetics.

Abstract explicitly states 'Germline BCOR mutations have been detected in patients with oculofaciocardiodental and Lenz microphthalmia syndromes', directly linking BCOR to inherited eye malformation syndromes. Also discusses BCOR fusion transcripts and somatic mutations in retinoblastoma. This is essential background on BCOR's known ophthalmic disease associations.

Directly reports pathogenic BCOR and PITX2 variants in Axenfeld-Rieger anomaly/syndrome, a primary anterior segment disorder. Abstract explicitly describes ARA, congenital glaucoma, corneal neovascularization, and cataracts associated with the identified variants. Core ophthalmogenetics content.

Study of inherited retinal diseases in 50 Turkish IRD patients identifies variants in ARSG and BBS12 genes among others, covering retinitis pigmentosa and Stargardt disease. Directly relevant to both genes catalogued (ARSG, BBS12) and to the library's retinal dystrophy focus.

Published in JCO Precision Oncology; describes BCOR alterations in pediatric sarcomas and high-grade glial malignancies. PubMed abstract is unavailable but journal, author affiliations (oncology departments), and title confirm an exclusively oncological focus with no ophthalmic content. BCOR's role here is as a cancer gene, not an eye disease gene.

Review explicitly titled 'Ocular phenotypes' for inherited metabolic disorders. Abstract describes 577 IMDs with ophthalmic manifestations including retinal degeneration, optic atrophy, corneal and lens involvement. Directly catalogues CERKL and IDH3A among the genes with ocular phenotypes.

Title 'Ceramide Signaling in Retinal Degeneration' directly maps to CERKL (Ceramide Kinase-Like), which causes retinitis pigmentosa. Even without an available abstract, the subject matter is precisely the molecular pathway implicated in CERKL-associated retinal disease. Relevant to the library.

Identifies RNU2-2 and RNU5B-1 as neurodevelopmental disorder genes through R-loop region analysis. Abstract and search keywords contain no ophthalmic terms. The paper characterises these spliceosomal RNA genes in the context of NDDs with no mention of retinal, corneal, or other ocular phenotypes. Insufficient connection to ophthalmogenetics.

Characterises 17beta-HSD6 and retinol dehydrogenase from rat and human prostate in the context of androgen/steroid metabolism. RDH11 is in the same enzyme superfamily but the paper's focus is prostate steroid biochemistry, not retinal biology. The retinol dehydrogenase mentioned (RoDH1) is a different enzyme than RDH11 and no retinal tissue is studied.

Describes purification and characterisation of retinol dehydrogenase from bovine RETINAL rod outer segments, with kinetics for all-trans retinol and retinal. This is foundational biochemistry for the retinaldehyde/visual cycle enzyme family to which RDH11 belongs, studied directly in retinal tissue.

Review of biochemical properties and biotechnological production of retinoids, focusing on industrial/microbial retinoid synthesis. Although retinol dehydrogenase is briefly reviewed and retinal's role in the visual cycle is mentioned, the paper's primary scope is biotechnology and metabolic engineering, not retinal pathology or inherited eye disease.

Generates iPSC lines from a retinitis pigmentosa patient carrying a homozygous CERKL c.769C>T (p.Arg257Ter) mutation. Directly studies CERKL-associated RP, provides disease-model cell lines for CERKL research. Core ophthalmogenetics content.

Clones and characterises liver microsomal retinol dehydrogenase (RoDH) expressed specifically in liver. The enzyme is studied in rat liver, not retinal tissue, in the context of hepatic retinoic acid biosynthesis. RDH11 is a related SDR family member but the paper does not study it or any retinal context.

General review of Polycomb PRC1/PR-DUB complexes in neurodevelopmental disorders and cancer. BCOR is a PRC1 component and would be catalogued in this review, but no ocular diseases, eye malformations, or ophthalmic phenotypes are mentioned in the abstract or MeSH terms (which cover Developmental Disabilities and Neoplasms). Insufficient ophthalmological relevance.

Review of Joubert syndrome, a ciliopathy in which LCA5 and RPGRIP1L are causative genes. PubMed MeSH terms include 'Eye Abnormalities' and 'Retina', and Joubert syndrome is well known to involve Leber congenital amaurosis and coloboma as ocular manifestations. Directly relevant to both genes listed.

Studies the molecular interaction between LC8 and LCA5 (lebercilin), the protein product of the Leber congenital amaurosis gene LCA5, in the ciliary-centrosome system. Provides mechanistic insight into LCA5 protein biology directly relevant to ciliopathy-related retinal degeneration.

Studies structural changes in the interphotoreceptor matrix during progressive rod-cone degeneration (prcd) in dogs using lectin cytochemistry. PRCD and IMPG1 (interphotoreceptor matrix glycoprotein 1) are both directly studied. The paper examines photoreceptor-matrix interactions in the PRCD disease model, relevant to both catalogued genes.

Establishes non-allelism of three early-onset hereditary retinal degeneration loci (rcd1, rcd2, erd) in dogs via cross-breeding experiments. These canine loci correspond to PDE6A (rcd1) and PRCD (erd/rcd2 lineage). Classic genetics paper establishing the genetic framework of retinal degeneration models for these genes.

Clinical review of albinism with detailed description of ocular features: foveal hypoplasia, reduced vision, nystagmus, positive angle kappa, strabismus, iris transillumination, absent melanin in fundi, and retinostriate decussation. LRMDA (OCA7) and TYR (OCA1) are both albinism genes directly discussed. Core ophthalmogenetics content.
